name: Shipping chokepoints
summary: Seafarer killed on a tanker hit in the Gulf on 5 Nov; UKMTO reports another waterline explosion near Oman
state: Velos Tankers said a crew member of the Velos Sapphire was killed after an explosion on 5 Nov, and UKMTO said a tanker leaving the strait near Oman reported an explosion at the waterline the same day (CBS News). Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two more tankers hit mines in or near Hormuz on 6 Nov, which maritime officials have not confirmed. Gas traders cite the attacks as a continuing risk to Gulf LNG (Trading Economics). Traffic remains materially impeded.
for_you: Expect continued delays and higher shipping and insurance costs on Gulf routes. For travel and maritime security follow FCDO advice and UKMTO notices.
rubric_hit: Hormuz traffic materially impeded by attacks and mines = Alert

sources.title: CBS News — Iran war updates: Trump touts imminent decision on new strikes
Gulf News — Trump signals 'heavy hit' as tankers catch fire near Hormuz

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
